question: What type of lens is a magnifying glass?
solution:
The correct answer is "__**Convex Lens**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Covex Lens**__ is a __**magnifying glass**__.

 __
 
• To make an** object** appear considerably **larger** than it actually is, a **magnifying glass** uses a convex lens. The object must be positioned so that its **distance** from the lens is **less** than the focal length for this to operate.
 
• In this manner, an upright, **virtual, and enlarged image** is created. Because **convex lenses** allow light rays to **converge**, or come together, a magnifying glass employs them to enlarge objects. Usually, a handle-equipped frame holding the lens is used.
 
• We can see that a concave lens causes the light beam from the source to diverge, which results in a virtual and decreased picture being generated. **Concave lenses cannot be used** as magnifying glasses, therefore.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 __**Lens**__
 __**Properties**__
 
 

 **Concave Lens**
 A **concave lens** is one that bends a straight light beam away from the source and focuses it into a distorted, upright virtual image. Both **actual and virtual images **can be created using it.
 
 

 **Parabolic Lens**
 The **parabolic lens** converts an arriving plane wave heading down the axis into a **spherical wave** convergent toward the focus.
 
 

 **Plane Lens**
 It is feasible to forecast the **course of light** rays via an optical system consisting of thick elements by using **plane lenses** to create a paraxial simplified model.
